newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent looking for supports to hold.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent looking for supports to hold.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
* The Brent market remains technically supported, but needs to hold above Monday's high and Friday's close of $20.35 to indicate further near term strength on the upside.
* The market will initially be looking for support levels to hold with overnight SIMEX and NYMEX futures both weaker.

IPE Brent crude oil futures were expected to continue consolidation but brokers and analysts said the market will initially be looking for support levels to hold with overnight SIMEX and NYMEX futures both weaker.
Some volatility was expected later today as traders square books ahead of the NYMEX June crude contract expiry at close of business.

Futures brokers said they expected some support for July Brent at around $20.01 a barrel, which represents a 50-percent retracement of the rally on Friday which took prices from a low of $19.43 to a high of $20.60 a barrel.
"I think we should expect some support around there," one broker said.
He said technically the market remained supported, but needed to hold above Monday's high and Friday's close of $20.35 to indicate further near term strength on the upside.
Al Graham of Elliott Wave International in Gainesville, Georgia said in his closing report for Monday that structural support for Brent lies around $20.06 down to $19.93 a barrel.
Any break of $20.33 structural resistance today would be a strong indication that Friday's $20.60 high is about to get vaporised.
"Just hang tough and stay bullish" said Graham.
On gas oil Graham expected prices to stay bullish exceeding $178.25 and a move towards $183 a tonne with the chart gap at $173.25 left unfilled.
U.K.-based independent consultant Elli Gifford took a more bearish short term view but saw the possibility of further gains in the longer term.

"The market is looking a bit toppy for the time being," she said. "Resistance at around $20.50 a barrel is pretty impressive and the market is currently overbought, to clear this level immediately looks unlikely."
"But in due course we could see the $21.50-85 range again," Gifford said.
Mees Pierson Derivatives said in there daily report the July Brent preparation had turned negative but saw a day of balanced trade within a small range.
For gas oil they said the market was overdue a selling extreme and recommended the market pay attention for the development of one today.
NYMEX crude futures ended lower across the board in active dealings, taking heating oil and unleaded gasoline down as well as the markets consolidated sharp gains posted last week.

July crude dropped 28 cents to settle at $21.90 a barrel, traded between $22.15 and $21.81. June unleaded gas fell 0.66 cent to 65.21 a gallon, while heating oil futures lost 0.55, closing at 57.92 a gallon.
The expiry of the June crude contract led trading in the complex, traders said, noting little fundamental news to thwart the inevitable profit taking after Friday's rally.
-- Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
